newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei ends up but firm dollar caps upside.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei ends up but firm dollar caps upside.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures ended up on Friday, underpinned by Wall Street but dealers said the upside was capped by the continued strength of the dollar and concerns over the health of Japan's financial sector.
Dealers said the Nikkei 225 March contract, plagued by Japanese banking woes and the firm dollar against the yen, had trouble breaching the 18,800 level.
The contract ended at 18,750, up 15 points after touching a high of 18,920. Turnover was at 20,215 lots.
Assurances by Japan's finance minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka that the government would protect depositors against problems at financial institutions helped underpin the market, dealers said.
"But the firmer dollar/yen is not good for the Nikkei now because it will hurt the banks and banking stocks will be sold down. That will cap Nikkei," said a dealer with a Japanese bank.
The March contract was expected to test 19,000 level next week if Wall Street sustains recent gains.
"If 19,000 is broken, then we should see the contract going towards 19,500," said the dealer.
The March MSCI Taiwan stock index contract ended down 0.2 points at 318.6 against its opening 319.0 on 252 lots.
